review.reason: Reject: the statement is unimplementable as written because it omits the invariants that make read-through caching of a token store safe. (a) Correctness — with no stated invalidation/ownership contract, a read-through cache serves stale or revoked credentials: the token store is written by refresh and revocation paths that bypass the cache, so a cached entry can outlive its TTL or serve a token after logout/revocation. Single-flight de-duplication additionally makes callers share one in-flight result, so an error or rejection for that one fetch (e.g. one 4xx from an upstream refresh) is fanned out to every waiting caller instead of each caller getting its own outcome, and a failure anywhere in the flight can be cached as the shared answer if negative results are not explicitly excluded. (b) Operational — no TTL/staleness bound, no explicit bypass or forced-refresh path for security-sensitive paths (revocation, rotation, impersonation), no metrics or hit/miss/eviction observability, and no bound on the single-flight map: a stalled fetch plus unbounded distinct keys turns de-duplication into a memory leak and head-of-line blocking that pins all waiters to one slow upstream. Concrete fix needed before I can defend this: state the cache key and invalidation trigger (write-through or explicit purge on every mutation, including revocation), a maximum staleness/TTL with a refresh path, that single-flight shares only successful results and propagates/permits retry on failure, and bounds plus metrics on the in-flight map.
